title: Rivers
source: Courses from OpenStreetMap (relations and named ways, by id); tributaries and distributaries after the notes' Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna, Kaveri, Brahmaputra, Ganga, Indus, Narmada, Tapi, Mahi and Luni maps

places.name: Godavari

source.name: Trambakeshwar
source.significance: Where the Godavari rises, in the Brahmagiri hills of the Western Ghats near Nashik

places.significance: The longest river of the peninsula — the 'Dakshin Ganga' — rising in the Western Ghats near Nashik and crossing the whole Deccan to the Bay of Bengal
notes: Rises at Trambakeshwar in the Brahmagiri hills, near Nashik (Maharashtra)
Flows through Maharashtra, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; its basin also drains Chhattisgarh and Odisha
Splits below Rajahmundry, at Dowleswaram, into the Gautami and the Vasishta, which build its delta

places.name: Gautami Godavari
places.significance: The eastern of the two great delta branches from Dowleswaram, reaching the sea near Yanam

places.name: Vasishta Godavari
places.significance: The western delta branch from Dowleswaram, reaching the sea at Antarvedi

places.name: Pravara
places.significance: Right-bank tributary from the Western Ghats near Ratangad, dammed at Bhandardara, meeting its parent near Newasa

places.name: Mula
places.significance: Rises in the Harishchandragad hills and is dammed at Rahuri before joining the Pravara near Newasa
notes: A tributary of the Pravara, not of the Godavari directly

places.name: Manjara
places.significance: Right-bank tributary from the Balaghat range in Beed, past Latur and the Nizam Sagar dam, joining near Kandakurthi in Telangana

places.name: Maner
places.significance: Telangana tributary through Karimnagar, dammed above the city, joining near Manthani

places.name: Kinnarsani
places.significance: Comes down from the forests of Bhadradri Kothagudem, whose wildlife sanctuary carries its name, to join near Bhadrachalam

places.name: Purna
places.significance: Left-bank tributary rising in the Ajanta range and draining Marathwada through Jalna and Parbhani — not the Tapi's river of the same name
notes: Rises in the Ajanta range

places.name: Dudhna
places.significance: Rises in the Ajanta hills near Aurangabad and joins the Purna in Parbhani district
notes: A tributary of the Purna

places.name: Penganga
places.significance: Rises in the Ajanta range in Buldhana and forms much of the Maharashtra–Telangana border before joining the Wardha
notes: A tributary of the Wardha

places.name: Wardha
places.significance: Rises in the Satpura range near Multai in Betul, gathers the Penganga, and with the Wainganga forms the Pranhita

places.name: Wainganga
places.significance: Rises in the Mahadeo Hills of Seoni and flows south past Bhandara and Gadchiroli; with the Wardha it forms the Pranhita

places.name: Kanhan
places.significance: Flows past the north of Nagpur, gathering the Pench, into the Wainganga
notes: Drawn only to carry the Pench to the Wainganga; never asked

places.name: Pench
places.significance: Rises in the Mahadeo Hills of Chhindwara and runs through the Seoni forests of the Jungle Book to join the Kanhan above Nagpur
notes: A tributary of the Kanhan, which carries it to the Wainganga

places.name: Pranhita
places.significance: The Wardha and the Wainganga combined — the largest tributary of all, meeting its parent at Kaleshwaram on the Maharashtra–Telangana border

places.name: Narangi
places.significance: A Bastar stream from the Kondagaon plateau, joining the Indravati
notes: A tributary of the Indravati

places.name: Indravati
places.significance: Rises in Odisha's Kalahandi and crosses Bastar over the Chitrakote Falls — 'India's Niagara' — to join where Maharashtra, Telangana and Chhattisgarh meet

places.name: Sabari
places.significance: Known in Odisha as the Kolab, it forms the Chhattisgarh–Odisha border and joins near Kunavaram above the Papi Hills gorge

places.name: Sileru
places.significance: Runs along the Andhra–Odisha border, its falls and dams harnessed for hydel power, to join the Sabari at Motu
notes: A tributary of the Sabari

places.name: Mahanadi

source.name: Sihawa
source.significance: Where the Mahanadi rises, in the hills of Chhattisgarh's Dhamtari district

places.significance: Rises near Sihawa in Chhattisgarh's Dhamtari district and is held back at Hirakud — one of the world's longest earthen dams — before its delta at Cuttack
notes: Rises near Sihawa (Dhamtari district, Chhattisgarh)
Flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha to the Bay of Bengal

places.name: Seonath
places.significance: The longest tributary, rising in Rajnandgaon and passing Durg to join at Shivrinarayan

places.name: Hasdo
places.significance: Flows south through the Korba coalfield, dammed at Bango, to join near Shivrinarayan

places.name: Mand
places.significance: Left-bank tributary from the Raigarh hills, joining near Chandrapur in Janjgir-Champa

places.name: Ib
places.significance: Rises in Jashpur's hills and empties into the reservoir behind Hirakud dam; its valley holds one of Odisha's main coalfields

places.name: Jonk
places.significance: Right-bank tributary from the Odisha border hills, flowing north through Mahasamund to join at Shivrinarayan

places.name: Ong
places.significance: Right-bank tributary through Bargarh district, joining above Sonepur

places.name: Tel
places.significance: The largest right-bank tributary, draining Kalahandi and Nabarangpur to join at Sonepur, Odisha's temple town

places.name: Kathajodi
places.significance: Branches off at Naraj above Cuttack and carries much of the delta's water past the city's south side

places.name: Devi
places.significance: A delta branch reaching the Bay of Bengal near Astaranga, where Olive Ridley turtles come ashore to nest
notes: Leaves the Kathajodi below Cuttack — a distributary, carrying water away from the main river to the sea

places.name: Krishna

source.name: Mahabaleshwar
source.significance: Where the Krishna rises, a hill station high in the Western Ghats of Satara district

places.significance: The peninsula's second-longest river, crossing the Deccan from the Western Ghats to the Bay of Bengal, held back at Almatti, Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar
notes: Rises at Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats (Satara, Maharashtra)
Flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh to the Bay of Bengal

places.name: Koyna
places.significance: Rises at Mahabaleshwar and powers Maharashtra's largest hydroelectric project before joining at Karad's Preeti Sangam

places.name: Varna
places.significance: Dammed at Chandoli in the Sahyadri, it runs along the Sangli–Kolhapur border to join at Haripur near Sangli

places.name: Panchganga
places.significance: Five streams meeting at Prayag Chikhali give Kolhapur its river, which joins at Narsobawadi, a Dattatreya pilgrimage town

places.name: Dudhganga
places.significance: Dammed at Kalammawadi in Kolhapur's hills, it crosses into Karnataka's Belagavi district to join

places.name: Ghatprabha
places.significance: Plunges over the Gokak Falls — the 'Niagara of Karnataka' — and is dammed at Hidkal before joining in Bagalkot

places.name: Malprabha
places.significance: Rises near Kanakumbi in the Western Ghats, is dammed at Navilutheertha, and joins at Kudalasangama, where Basavanna rests

places.name: Bhima
places.significance: Rises at a Jyotirlinga shrine in the Sahyadri above Pune, flows past the pilgrim town of Pandharpur, and joins near Raichur

places.name: Nira
places.significance: Rises in the Sahyadri near Bhor and divides Pune district from Satara before joining at Narsinghpur

places.name: Man
places.significance: Drains the drought-prone Mandesh of eastern Satara and Sangli to join near Pandharpur

places.name: Sina
places.significance: Rises near Ahmednagar and flows south-east through Solapur district to join at Kudal

places.name: Tungabhadra
places.significance: The Tunga and the Bhadra combined from Koodli, past Hampi and the Hosapete dam, to join near Alampur
notes: Drawn only to carry the Tunga and the Bhadra to the Krishna; never asked

places.name: Tunga
places.significance: Rises at Gangamoola in the Kudremukh hills and flows past Sringeri and Shivamogga to meet its twin at Koodli

places.name: Bhadra
places.significance: Rises at Gangamoola beside its twin, is dammed at Lakkavalli, and meets it at Koodli to form the river that carries both to the Krishna

places.name: Musi
places.significance: Hyderabad's river, on whose banks the city was founded, dammed at Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar above it, joining at Wazirabad

places.name: Munneru
places.significance: Comes down from the hills of Mahabubabad past Khammam to join above Vijayawada

places.name: Kaveri

source.name: Talakaveri
source.significance: Where the Kaveri rises, a sacred spring high in the hills of Kodagu on the Western Ghats

places.significance: The south's most disputed river, shared by Karnataka and Tamil Nadu: dammed at Krishnaraja Sagar and Mettur, falling at Shivanasamudra and Hogenakkal, and spreading into the Thanjavur delta
notes: Rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu (Karnataka)
Flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu to the Bay of Bengal

places.name: Hemavati
places.significance: Rises at Ballalarayanadurga in the Western Ghats of Chikkamagaluru, is dammed at Gorur, and joins near Krishnarajapete above the great reservoir

places.name: Shimsha
places.significance: Rises in Tumakuru's Devarayanadurga hills, flows past Maddur, and drops through a hydel cascade beside Shivanasamudra to join

places.name: Arkavati
places.significance: Bengaluru's old water supply, dammed at Hesaraghatta and Thippagondanahalli, joining at Sangama near Mekedatu

places.name: Lakshmantirtha
places.significance: Tumbles over the Iruppu Falls in southern Kodagu and joins at the Krishnaraja Sagar reservoir

places.name: Kabini
places.significance: Rises in Kerala's Wayanad and is dammed at Beechanahalli between the Nagarhole and Bandipur forests, joining at Tirumakudalu Narasipura

places.name: Suvarnavati
places.significance: Chamarajanagar district's river, flowing north past Yelandur to join near Kollegal

places.name: Bhavani
places.significance: Rises in the Nilgiris beside Kerala's Silent Valley, is held back by one of Asia's largest earthen dams, and joins at Kooduthurai in Erode

places.name: Noyyal
places.significance: Coimbatore's river, and Tiruppur's — dyed by the knitwear town's factories — joining near Kodumudi

places.name: Amaravati
places.significance: Rises in the Anaimalai hills, flows past Dharapuram, and joins at Karur

places.name: Thirumanimuthar
places.significance: Rises in Salem's Shevaroy hills and drains the city before joining near Paramathi Velur in Namakkal

places.name: Brahmaputra

source.name: Chemayungdung Glacier
source.significance: Where the Brahmaputra rises, in the Kailash range of Tibet south-east of Lake Mansarovar

places.significance: Crosses the roof of the world, bends round Namcha Barwa through the deepest gorge on Earth, and floods Assam's plain every monsoon before meeting the Padma (Ganga) in Bangladesh
notes: 1. **Tibet** → River: Yarlung Tsangpo, Origin: Chemayungdung Glacier
2. **Arunachal Pradesh** → Associated rivers: Dihang/Dibang, Pass: Yongyab Pass, Mountain: Namcha Barwa
3. **Assam** → Called the Sorrow of Assam, Island: Majuli
4. **Bangladesh** → Known as the **Jamuna**, which further becomes the **Meghna**, Delta: Sundarban delta

places.name: Subansiri
places.significance: Its largest tributary, rising in Tibet and cutting through Arunachal to join beside Majuli; dammed at Gerukamukh for India's biggest hydro project

places.name: Kameng
places.significance: Rises below Gori Chen on the Tawang border and runs past the Pakke tiger reserve, taking another name in Assam to join near Tezpur

places.name: Manas
places.significance: Comes down from Bhutan through a World Heritage tiger reserve on the border to join at Jogighopa

places.name: Gangadhar
places.significance: The Sankosh and the Raidak combined, from the Assam–West Bengal border into Bangladesh to meet the main stream
notes: Drawn only to carry the Sankosh and the Raidak to the Brahmaputra; never asked

places.name: Sankosh
places.significance: Rises in northern Bhutan, flows past Punakha's dzong, and forms the Assam–West Bengal border before joining near Bangladesh

places.name: Raidak
places.significance: Flows past Bhutan's capital, Thimphu, and the Chukha hydro project before crossing Alipurduar into Bangladesh

places.name: Jaldhaka
places.significance: Rises in the lakes of eastern Sikkim and crosses the Dooars, harnessed at Jhalong, on its way into Bangladesh

places.name: Teesta

source.name: Tso Lhamo Lake
source.significance: Where the Teesta rises, among the ice and high lakes of north Sikkim near the Tibet border

places.significance: Sikkim's lifeline, carving the state from north to south before crossing the Siliguri plain into Bangladesh, where sharing its water is a long dispute
notes: Rises at Zemu Glacier / Tso Lhamo Lake in north Sikkim

places.name: Rangit
places.significance: Sikkim's western river, from the glaciers below Kanchenjunga, meeting its parent at Melli below Darjeeling

places.name: Dibang
places.significance: Comes down from the Mishmi Hills of Arunachal, where India's tallest dam is being built, to meet its neighbour near Sadiya just above the main stream

places.name: Lohit
places.significance: The 'river of blood', named for the red earth it carries, entering India from Tibet at Kibithu and passing the pilgrim pool of Parshuram Kund
notes: Known as the river of blood (the red river)

places.name: Burhi Dihing
places.significance: Rises in the Patkai hills and runs past Digboi's century-old oilfield and the rainforest at Jeypore

places.name: Dhansiri
places.significance: Rises in Nagaland's hills and flows past Dimapur and Golaghat to join

places.name: Kopili
places.significance: Rises in Meghalaya's Jaintia hills, is harnessed at Umrangso for hydel power, and joins in Morigaon district

places.name: Majuli
places.significance: The world's largest river island, home to Assam's Vaishnavite satras, and shrinking with every monsoon flood
notes: In the Brahmaputra in Assam, between the main stream and the Subansiri

places.name: Namcha Barwa
places.significance: The 7,782m summit in Tibet round which the main stream makes its great bend south into India, through the deepest gorge on Earth

places.name: Ganga
places.significance: India's most sacred river and the lifeline of the northern plains, born where two Garhwal headstreams meet and carrying Himalayan snowmelt past Varanasi and Patna to the world's largest delta
notes: Flows through five states: **Uttarakhand**, **Uttar Pradesh**, **Bihar**, **Jharkhand** and **West Bengal**
Called the **Padma** in Bangladesh
In Bangladesh the Padma meets the **Jamuna** (the Brahmaputra), then the **Meghna**, and reaches the Bay of Bengal as the Meghna

places.name: Bhagirathi
places.significance: The headstream held to be the true source, rising above Gangotri's temple in Uttarkashi and dammed at Tehri on its way to Devprayag
notes: Rises at the Gangotri Glacier, at Gaumukh
Dammed at Tehri
Meets the Alaknanda at **Devprayag**: from there the river is the Ganga

source.name: Gangotri Glacier
source.significance: Where the Bhagirathi rises: the ice-cave snout pilgrims trek to above Uttarkashi's temple town, the 'cow's mouth'

places.name: Alaknanda
places.significance: The longer headstream, coming down past Badrinath and gathering four rivers at four of Garhwal's five sacred confluences
notes: Rises at the Satopanth Glacier, near Badrinath
Joined by the Dhauliganga at **Vishnuprayag**, the Nandakini at **Nandprayag**, the Pindar at **Karnaprayag** and the Mandakini at **Rudraprayag**
Meets the Bhagirathi at **Devprayag**: from there the river is the Ganga

source.name: Satopanth Glacier
source.significance: Where the Alaknanda rises, in the ice behind Badrinath and the village of Mana

places.name: Dhauliganga
places.significance: Comes down from the Niti pass on the Tibet border past Tapovan, the valley of the 2021 Chamoli flood
notes: Joins the Alaknanda at **Vishnuprayag**

places.name: Nandakini
places.significance: A short Chamoli stream from the slopes below Trishul and Nanda Ghunti
notes: Joins the Alaknanda at **Nandprayag**

places.name: Pindar
places.significance: Comes off a Kumaon glacier at the head of a famous trek from Bageshwar, and crosses into Garhwal
notes: Rises at the Pindari Glacier
Joins the Alaknanda at **Karnaprayag**

places.name: Mandakini
places.significance: Flows from Kedarnath down the valley the 2013 cloudburst flood tore through, past Sonprayag and Guptkashi
notes: Rises at the Chorabari Glacier, near Kedarnath
Joins the Alaknanda at **Rudraprayag**

source.name: Chorabari Glacier
source.significance: Where the Mandakini rises, just above the Kedarnath temple — its lake burst in the 2013 flood

places.name: Ramganga
places.significance: Rises in Garhwal's Dudhatoli hills, is dammed at Kalagarh inside Corbett National Park, and crosses Rohilkhand past Moradabad and Bareilly
notes: Flows past **Moradabad**
Joins the Ganga near Kannauj

places.name: Gomti
places.significance: Lucknow's river, fed by groundwater and rain rather than snow, meeting the main stream below Varanasi
notes: Rises at Fulhar Jheel (Gomat Taal), Pilibhit
Flows past **Lucknow**
Tributary: Sai
Joins the Ganga at **Saidpur–Kaithi** (Ghazipur)

source.name: Fulhar Jheel
source.significance: Where the Gomti rises, a lake near Madhotanda in Pilibhit district of Uttar Pradesh

places.name: Sai
places.significance: Rises in Hardoi and flows past Rae Bareli and Pratapgarh to meet its parent near Jaunpur

places.name: Ghaghra
places.significance: Rises in Tibet, crosses Nepal as its longest river, and flows past Ayodhya to the plain of Bihar
notes: Rises at the Mapchachungo Glacier in Tibet
!!Called the Karnali in Nepal; tributaries there: Seti, Tila and Bheri!!
Joined by the Kali (Sharda), which forms the India–Nepal border, and by the Rapti
Flows past **Bahraich**
Joins the Ganga near **Chhapra**

source.name: Mapchachungo Glacier
source.significance: Where the Ghaghra rises, in Tibet south-west of Lake Mansarovar, near the Indian border

places.name: Seti
places.significance: Drains far-western Nepal from the Saipal Himal, joining the main stream in its gorge
notes: In Nepal
Joins the Karnali (Ghaghra)

places.name: Tila
places.significance: Flows through Jumla, home of the world's highest rice paddies, in Nepal's far west
notes: In Nepal
Joins the Karnali (Ghaghra)

places.name: Bheri
places.significance: The largest feeder of Nepal's longest river, coming down from Dolpo through Jajarkot and Surkhet
notes: In Nepal
Joins the Karnali (Ghaghra)

places.name: Kali
places.significance: The border river between Uttarakhand and Nepal from its source below the Lipulekh pass, until it reaches the plains at the Banbasa barrage
notes: Rises at Kalapani, below the Lipulekh pass
Forms the India–Nepal border along Uttarakhand
Called the **Sharda** in the plains
Joins the Ghaghra

places.name: Rapti
places.significance: Rises in Nepal's Rolpa hills and floods Gorakhpur almost every monsoon
notes: Flows past **Gorakhpur**
Joins the Ghaghra

places.name: Gandak
places.significance: Rises on the Tibetan edge of Mustang, cuts between Dhaulagiri and Annapurna, and enters India at the Valmikinagar barrage
notes: Called the **Gandaki** and the **Narayani** in Nepal; tributary there: Trishuli
Joins the Ganga at **Sonepur**, opposite Patna

places.name: Trishuli
places.significance: Comes down from the Kyirong crossing on the Tibet border, along the main road north from Kathmandu
notes: In Nepal
Joins the Gandaki (Gandak)

places.name: Burhi Gandak
places.significance: Runs parallel to its larger namesake across north Bihar, past Motihari, Muzaffarpur and Samastipur
notes: Flows past Muzaffarpur
Joins the Ganga near **Khagaria**

places.name: Kosi
places.significance: The 'Sorrow of Bihar', which has swung its course over 100km westward in two centuries and breached its embankment at Kusaha in 2008
notes: Called the **Sorrow of Bihar**
Formed in Nepal by the Sunkoshi, the Arun and the Tamor
Joins the Ganga near Kursela (Katihar)

places.name: Sunkoshi
places.significance: Flows east below Nepal's Mahabharat range, gathering the rivers that drain Everest's Khumbu
notes: In Nepal
Meets the Arun and the Tamor to form the Kosi

places.name: Arun
places.significance: Rises in Tibet north of the Himalaya and cuts clean through the range between Everest and Kanchenjunga — an antecedent river, older than the mountains
notes: Rises in Tibet; through Nepal
Meets the Sunkoshi and the Tamor to form the Kosi

places.name: Tamor
places.significance: The eastern of the three headstreams, draining the Kanchenjunga massif in far-eastern Nepal
notes: In Nepal
Meets the Sunkoshi and the Arun to form the Kosi

places.name: Mahananda
places.significance: Rises in the Darjeeling hills near Kurseong, runs past Siliguri and Malda, and meets the main stream in Bangladesh
notes: Tributary: Mechi
Joins the Ganga (the Padma) in Bangladesh, near Godagari

places.name: Mechi
places.significance: Marks the India–Nepal border at Nepal's eastern edge, below Kakarbhitta
notes: Forms part of the India–Nepal border
Joins the Mahananda

places.name: Yamuna
places.significance: The Ganga's longest tributary, past Delhi, Mathura and Agra's Taj Mahal, meeting it at the Sangam
notes: Rises at the Yamunotri Glacier on Bandarpunch
Right-bank tributaries: Chambal, Sindh, Betwa and Ken
Joins the Ganga at **Prayagraj** (the Triveni Sangam)

source.name: Yamunotri Glacier
source.significance: Where the Yamuna rises, on the slopes of Bandarpunch in Uttarkashi

places.name: Chambal
places.significance: Cuts the ravines of the old dacoit badlands and shelters the gharial in its own sanctuary on its way to the Pachnada
notes: Rises at Janapav, near Mhow (Malwa Plateau)
Tributaries: Banas, Kuno, Parbati, Kali Sindh and Shipra (with the Gambhir)
Joins the Yamuna at **Bhareh**, Etawah (UP)

source.name: Janapav
source.significance: Where the Chambal rises, a Vindhyan summit near Mhow on the Malwa Plateau, south-west of Indore

places.name: Banas
places.significance: The one major river that runs its whole course inside Rajasthan, rising in the Aravallis near Kumbhalgarh

places.name: Kuno
places.significance: Gives its name to the national park where India brought cheetahs back in 2022

places.name: Parbati
places.significance: Rises in the Vindhyas of Sehore and runs along the Rajasthan–Madhya Pradesh border before its mouth near Pali

places.name: Kali Sindh
places.significance: Rises near Dewas on the Malwa Plateau and flows north through Jhalawar into Rajasthan's Hadoti

places.name: Shipra
places.significance: Ujjain's sacred river, on whose ghats the Simhastha Kumbh is held every twelve years

places.name: Gambhir
places.significance: Rises near Indore and is dammed at Yashwant Sagar, a source of the city's water
notes: Joins the Shipra, which carries it on to the Chambal

places.name: Sindh
places.significance: Rises on the Malwa Plateau in Vidisha and flows north past Datia to the Pachnada, the meeting of five rivers
notes: Joins the Yamuna near Etawah, beside the Chambal's mouth

places.name: Betwa
places.significance: Flows past Orchha's cenotaphs and is dammed at Rajghat and Matatila on its way through Bundelkhand
notes: Rises in the Vindhyan Range near Bhopal
Joins the Yamuna at **Hamirpur**

source.name: Vindhyan Range
source.significance: Where the Betwa rises, in the hills just south of Bhopal

places.name: Ken
places.significance: Flows through Panna's tiger reserve, and is to be joined to the Betwa by India's first river-interlinking project
notes: Rises in Katni district, in the Kaimur Range
Joins the Yamuna at **Chilla** village (Banda)

source.name: Kaimur Range
source.significance: Where the Ken rises, in the uplands of Katni district in Madhya Pradesh

places.name: Son
places.significance: Rises on the Amarkantak plateau beside the Narmada but flows the other way, north and then east, to the plain near Patna
notes: Tributaries: Johilla, Rihand and North Koel
Passes Sonbhadra (UP)
Joins the Ganga near **Patna**

places.name: Johilla
places.significance: A short stream from the Maikal hills near Amarkantak, flowing north through Umaria

places.name: Rihand
places.significance: Dammed at Pipri into the Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar, whose water cools the power stations of Singrauli
notes: Joins the Son in **Sonbhadra** (UP)

places.name: North Koel
places.significance: Drains Jharkhand's Palamu and the forests of Betla, and is dammed at Mandal

places.name: Ganga (Patna channel)
places.significance: The old southern channel along the Bihar capital's ghats, where the Punpun comes in
notes: Drawn only to carry the Punpun to the main stream; never asked

places.name: Harohar
places.significance: Gathers the water of the Mokama Tal wetlands and carries it east to the main stream near Surajgarha
notes: Drawn only to carry the Phalgu to the Ganga; never asked

places.name: Punpun
places.significance: A south Bihar river that waters the Patna plain's paddy and reaches the main stream at Fatuha, below the capital
notes: Joins the Ganga at Fatuha, below Patna

places.name: Phalgu
places.significance: Gaya's sacred river, dry sand for most of the year, where pilgrims offer pind-daan to their ancestors
notes: Flows past **Gaya** and Bodh Gaya
Its water reaches the Ganga through the Harohar

places.name: Hooghly
places.significance: Leaves the main stream in West Bengal to carry Kolkata's port traffic to the sea, kept flowing by the Farakka barrage's feeder canal
notes: A distributary: leaves the Ganga in Murshidabad and reaches the Bay of Bengal
Kolkata stands on it
The Damodar joins it below Kolkata

places.name: Damodar
places.significance: Flows through India's richest coal belt — Jharia, Bokaro, Raniganj — and was tamed by the country's first multipurpose river valley project
notes: Rises on the Chota Nagpur Plateau
Joins the Hooghly below Kolkata

source.name: Chota Nagpur Plateau
source.significance: Where the Damodar rises, in the hills of Latehar district in Jharkhand

places.name: Meghna
places.significance: The Surma's way on to the Padma at Chandpur
notes: Drawn only to carry the Surma to the Padma; never asked

places.name: Surma
places.significance: Flows past Sylhet's tea gardens through north-eastern Bangladesh, the Barak's continuation from Assam
notes: In Bangladesh: the Barak of Manipur and Assam, split at the border into the Surma and the Kushiyara
Reaches the Meghna through the Ghorautra

places.name: Vishnuprayag
places.significance: Where the Dhauliganga joins the Alaknanda below Joshimath — the first of Garhwal's five sacred confluences

places.name: Nandprayag
places.significance: Where the Nandakini joins the Alaknanda in Chamoli — the second of the five sacred confluences

places.name: Karnaprayag
places.significance: Where the Pindar joins the Alaknanda — the third of the five sacred confluences, and the railhead the line from Rishikesh is being built to

places.name: Rudraprayag
places.significance: Where the Mandakini from Kedarnath joins the Alaknanda — the fourth of the five, once terrorised by the leopard Jim Corbett shot in 1926

places.name: Devprayag
places.significance: Where the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda and the river takes the name Ganga — the last of the five sacred confluences

places.name: Prayagraj
places.significance: Where the Yamuna joins the Ganga with the unseen Saraswati — the three-river meeting that hosts the Kumbh Mela

places.name: Bhareh
places.significance: Where the Chambal joins the Yamuna in Etawah district of Uttar Pradesh, beside the Pachnada

places.name: Hamirpur
places.significance: Where the Betwa joins the Yamuna, at the head of Uttar Pradesh's Bundelkhand

places.name: Chilla
places.significance: Where the Ken joins the Yamuna, a village in Banda district of Uttar Pradesh

places.name: Kaithi
places.significance: Where the Gomti joins the Ganga near Ghazipur, beside the Markandeya Mahadev temple

places.name: Chhapra
places.significance: Where the Ghaghra joins the Ganga, at the headquarters of Bihar's Saran district

places.name: Sonepur
places.significance: Where the Gandak joins the Ganga opposite Patna — the site of Asia's largest cattle fair

places.name: Khagaria
places.significance: Where the Burhi Gandak joins the Ganga, in a flood-prone north Bihar district ringed by rivers

places.name: Indus
places.significance: The river that gave India its name, cradle of the Harappan civilisation, crossing Ladakh and Gilgit-Baltistan before it waters all of Pakistan; its system is shared under the 1960 water treaty
notes: Rises at **Bokhar Chu** in Tibet, north of Mansarovar, as the Singhi Khamban (the Lion's Mouth)
Enters India in Ladakh at Demchok and flows past **Leh** between the Ladakh and Zaskar ranges
Bends south round Nanga Parbat in Gilgit-Baltistan
Joined at **Panchnad**, near Mithankot, by the five rivers of the Punjab as one stream
Reaches the Arabian Sea in Sindh, south-east of Karachi

source.name: Bokhar Chu
source.significance: Where the Indus rises, a glacier spring on the Tibetan plateau north of Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar

places.name: Shyok
places.significance: Rises at the Rimo Glacier below the Karakoram Pass and runs along the Line of Actual Control into Baltistan; the road to Daulat Beg Oldi, India's northernmost post, follows its valley
notes: Rises at the Rimo Glacier in the Karakoram
Joined by the **Nubra** and the **Galwan**
Joins the Indus in Baltistan, above Skardu

places.name: Nubra
places.significance: Carries the meltwater of the Siachen Glacier, the world's highest battlefield, through a valley of sand dunes and Bactrian camels north of the Khardung La
notes: Rises at the snout of the Siachen Glacier
Joins the Shyok at Diskit

places.name: Galwan
places.significance: A short stream out of Aksai Chin whose valley saw the June 2020 clash between Indian and Chinese troops on the Line of Actual Control
notes: Flows west out of Aksai Chin
Joins the Shyok

places.name: Shigar
places.significance: Carries the meltwater of the Baltoro and Biafo glaciers, below K2, down a broad valley to Skardu
notes: Fed by the Braldu, from the Baltoro Glacier below K2
Joins the Indus at Skardu

places.name: Hunza
places.significance: Flows down from the Khunjerab Pass past Karimabad, with the Karakoram Highway along its valley, and was dammed for five years by the Attabad landslide
notes: The Karakoram Highway follows it from the Khunjerab Pass
Joins the Gilgit at Gilgit town

places.name: Gilgit
places.significance: Drains the eastern Hindu Kush from the Shandur Pass and meets the main stream near Bunji, where the Himalaya, the Karakoram and the Hindu Kush meet
notes: Rises near the Shandur Pass
Joined by the **Hunza**
Joins the Indus near Bunji

places.name: Zanskar
places.significance: Its frozen winter gorge is the Chadar trek, for months the only way out of Padum, before it meets the main stream at Nimmu below Leh
notes: Joins the Indus at Nimmu, below Leh
Frozen in winter: the Chadar trek

places.name: Dras
places.significance: Rises near the Zoji La and flows through the town called India's coldest inhabited place, below Tololing and Tiger Hill of the 1999 Kargil war
notes: Rises near the Zoji La
Joined by the Suru at Kargil, it meets the Indus at Marol

places.name: Kishanganga
places.significance: Rises near Sonamarg, runs along and across the Line of Control past Gurez to Muzaffarabad; India's dam on it was upheld by the Hague Court of Arbitration in 2013
notes: Called the **Neelum** in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir
Joins the Jhelum at Muzaffarabad

places.name: Jhelum
places.significance: The river of the Kashmir Valley, winding through Srinagar and Wular Lake before it cuts a gorge to Muzaffarabad and the plains of Pakistan
notes: Rises at **Verinag**, a spring at the foot of the Pir Panjal
Flows through **Srinagar** and Wular Lake
Joins the Chenab at Trimmu in Pakistan

source.name: Verinag
source.significance: Where the Jhelum rises: a spring in an octagonal Mughal tank built by Jahangir, at the foot of the Pir Panjal in Anantnag

places.name: Poonch
places.significance: Rises on the Pir Panjal and crosses the Line of Control to the Mangla reservoir, where it meets the main stream
notes: Rises on the Pir Panjal
Joins the Jhelum at the Mangla reservoir

places.name: Chenab
places.significance: The largest of the Punjab's rivers by volume, spanned at Reasi by the world's highest railway arch bridge and harnessed at Salal and Baglihar
notes: Formed at Tandi in Lahaul by the Chandra and the Bhaga; the Bhaga rises near **Baralacha La**
Flows past **Jammu** (at Akhnoor) into Pakistan
Joined by the Jhelum, the Ravi and the Sutlej; as the **Panjnad** it joins the Indus

source.name: Baralacha La
source.significance: Where the Chenab rises, through its headstream the Bhaga at Suraj Tal, on the pass from Lahaul to Ladakh

places.name: Ravi
places.significance: Flows past Chamba and Lahore and forms the India–Pakistan border for a stretch, held back at Thein by the Ranjit Sagar dam
notes: Rises in the **Bara Bangal** region of Kangra
Flows past Chamba, then along the Punjab border with Pakistan
Joins the Chenab in Pakistan

source.name: Bara Bangal
source.significance: Where the Ravi rises, a remote high valley of Kangra between the Dhauladhar and the Pir Panjal

places.name: Beas
places.significance: Runs through the Kullu valley past Manali and Mandi, is dammed at Pandoh and Pong, and is the one river of the five that flows wholly in India
notes: Rises at Beas Kund near **Rohtang Pass**
Dammed at Pandoh and at Pong (Maharana Pratap Sagar)
Joins the Sutlej at **Harike**

source.name: Rohtang Pass
source.significance: Where the Beas rises, at the Beas Kund spring below the pass from Manali over the Pir Panjal into Lahaul

places.name: Sutlej
places.significance: Breaks through the Himalaya from Tibet and drives the Bhakra Nangal and Nathpa Jhakri projects before the Indira Gandhi Canal carries its water into the Thar
notes: Rises at **Rakas Tal** (Langchen Khambab) beside Mansarovar in Tibet
Enters India at **Shipki La** in Kinnaur
Dammed at Bhakra (Gobind Sagar)
Joined by the Beas at Harike; joins the Chenab in Pakistan

source.name: Rakas Tal
source.significance: Where the Sutlej rises, the salt 'demons' lake' beside Mansarovar below Mount Kailash

places.name: Panchnad
places.significance: Where the five rivers of the Punjab, gathered into one stream, join the main stream near Mithankot in Pakistan

places.name: Pangong Tso
places.significance: A brackish lake 4,350m up in eastern Ladakh, two-thirds of it in Tibet, astride the Line of Actual Control — the scene of the 2020 standoff
notes: An endorheic lake: no river leaves it

places.name: Tso Moriri
places.significance: The largest high-altitude lake wholly in India, in Ladakh's Changthang at 4,500m — a Ramsar wetland where bar-headed geese breed

places.name: Shipki La
places.significance: The pass in Kinnaur where the Sutlej breaks through the Himalaya from Tibet into India, and a border trading post with China

places.name: Narmada
places.significance: The holiest river of central India, flowing west through a rift valley between the Vindhyas and the Satpuras to the Arabian Sea, and dammed at Sardar Sarovar
notes: Rises at **Amarkantak** on the Maikal Range
Flows west through a rift valley between the Vindhyas and the Satpuras
Cuts the Marble Rocks gorge and falls at Dhuandhar at Bhedaghat, near Jabalpur
Sardar Sarovar dam in Gujarat
!!Bharuch!! stands on its estuary, on the Gulf of Khambhat

source.name: Amarkantak
source.significance: Where the Narmada rises, a temple tank on the Maikal plateau where the Vindhyas meet the Satpuras, and where the Son rises too

places.name: Banjar
places.significance: Drains Kanha, the tiger reserve of the Maikal hills, before joining the main stream at Mandla
notes: Rises in the Maikal hills
Joins the Narmada at Mandla

places.name: Sher
places.significance: A Satpura stream from Seoni across the sugarcane country of Narsinghpur to the main stream
notes: Rises on the Satpura plateau in Seoni
Joins the Narmada in Narsinghpur district

places.name: Shakkar
places.significance: Comes down from the Satpuras of Chhindwara across Gadarwara's pulse and sugarcane fields to the main stream
notes: Rises in the Satpuras of Chhindwara
Joins the Narmada in Narsinghpur district

places.name: Tawa
places.significance: The longest tributary, rising near Pachmarhi in the Satpuras and dammed near Itarsi to irrigate the Hoshangabad plain
notes: Rises near Pachmarhi in the Satpuras
Joins the Narmada at Bandrabhan, near Hoshangabad (Narmadapuram)

places.name: Barna
places.significance: Rises in the Vindhyas of Raisen district and is dammed at Bari to irrigate the wheat fields above the main stream's valley
notes: Rises in the Vindhyas
Joins the Narmada in Raisen district

places.name: Kolar
places.significance: Rises in the Vindhyas of Sehore and is dammed to give Bhopal its drinking water before it joins the main stream
notes: Rises in the Vindhyas
Supplies Bhopal from its dam
Joins the Narmada in Sehore district

places.name: Hiran
places.significance: A right-bank stream from the Kaimur hills near Kundam, draining the Jabalpur–Narsinghpur plain below the Bhanrer range
notes: Rises in the Kaimur hills of Jabalpur district
Joins the Narmada in Narsinghpur district

places.name: Tapi
places.significance: Runs west in a rift valley of its own south of the Satpuras, parallel to its larger northern neighbour, to the Gulf of Khambhat
notes: Rises at **Multai** in Betul district, on the Satpura Range
Flows west through a rift valley, south of the Satpuras
Ukai dam in Gujarat
!!Surat!! stands on its estuary, on the Gulf of Khambhat

source.name: Multai
source.significance: Where the Tapi rises, a sacred tank in Betul district on the Satpura plateau of Madhya Pradesh

places.name: Mahi
places.significance: The one river crossed twice by the Tropic of Cancer, looping north through Rajasthan's Banswara before turning back south into Gujarat to the Gulf of Khambhat
notes: Rises at Minda in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh, on the Vindhyas
Crosses the **Tropic of Cancer** twice
Mahi Bajaj Sagar dam at Banswara in Rajasthan; Kadana dam in Gujarat
Reaches the Gulf of Khambhat

source.name: Minda
source.significance: Where the Mahi rises, by a village on the western Vindhyas in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh

places.name: Luni
places.significance: The Thar's only sizeable river, fresh near its source and salt below Balotra, and lost not in the sea but in the Rann of Kutch
notes: Rises near Pushkar in the Aravalli, west of Ajmer
The only big river of the Thar; its water turns saline below Balotra
An inland river: it never reaches the sea, but ends in the Rann of Kutch

source.name: Pushkar
source.significance: Where the Luni rises, in the Aravalli west of Ajmer, beside the lake town of the Brahma temple and the camel fair

groups.name: Kaveri — left-bank tributaries
groups.mnemonic: C̶ H S A T — CSAT with the C struck out for an H: Hemavati, Shimsha, Arkavati, Thirumanimuthar

groups.name: Kaveri — right-bank tributaries (L K S)
groups.mnemonic: L K S — Laksham ji Tirth se Kab aaye? Swarn hiran leke aaye: Lakshmantirtha, Kabini, Suvarnavati
